questions.q: Distinguish between tertiary, quaternary and quinary activities.
answer: As economies develop, activities beyond farming and manufacturing become more important, and these are grouped into tertiary, quaternary and quinary activities.

answer.text: Tertiary activities make up the service sector. Instead of producing goods, they provide services such as trade and commerce, transport, communication, banking, insurance, tourism, health and education. They rely on skills and labour rather than raw materials.

Quaternary activities form the knowledge sector, concerned with the collection, production and spread of information. They include research and development, information technology, consultancy and finance, and require highly trained people.

Quinary activities are the highest level, involving the making of important decisions and the use of specialised, high-level knowledge. They are carried out by top executives, policymakers and leading scientists, and are sometimes called gold-collar professions.

answer: Thus these activities move from providing everyday services to handling knowledge and taking key decisions.

questions.q: Why is the tertiary sector growing so rapidly in the modern economy?

answer.text: is growing fast across the world and now dominates many economies, for several reasons.

list: As incomes rise, people demand more services — health, education, entertainment, travel and finance
Advances in technology and communication have created many new services and made them tradable across the world
As farming and industry become more productive with machines, labour moves into services
Modern industry and trade also need many supporting services — transport, banking, insurance and IT — so the sector keeps expanding

questions.q: What are quaternary and quinary activities, and why are they important in a knowledge economy?

answer.text: the most advanced economies have quaternary and quinary activities based on knowledge and decision-making.

list: They include research and development, information technology and data processing
They create, handle and spread knowledge rather than tangible goods

answer.text: are the highest level of decision-making.

list: They involve top experts and executives — the 'gold-collar' professionals — who make high-level decisions and set policy
In a knowledge economy, these activities add the most value and drive innovation and growth
